My main gripe with this game is the revive system. In a group of 6, having it revive the person who died last is a pretty bad system. If player A dies, then the group finally gets enough bottles to revive a teammate (too many bottles to revive someone tbh) and then player B dies before revive goes off, then player B will be revived and player A is still waiting. In a smaller group it's not that bad, but in larger groups it's not ideal. Make it a little cheaper to revive someone or change it to revive the oldest deaths first. I'll change review when that system is updated.

So much missed potential, and it genuinely makes me sad that I have to refund after this game's amazing first impression. I cannot stress enough that the Ideas Guy™ for this game absolutely cooked and then some. It just sucks that the gameplay isn't fun in the slightest. Like, it's absolutely criminal how they had all the ingredients for a smash hit, only for it to be so extremely boring. Though me and my friend did only get to like floor 10 before we decided on refunding, so bear that in mind. + Graphics and sound design are great. Everything is grimy and fleshy, and it's like you can hear the whole complex creaking around you. The first few levels feel claustrophobic in a good way, because it really does make you feel like you're some random prisoner sentenced to an inescapable suicide mission. +++ Getting assigned random bonus stats based off of whatever crimes you're convicted of is absolutely genius game design. Shame that many of those stats don't really feel that impactful in moment to moment gameplay. Enemies getting pushed back or crates instantly breaking when you run into them, now that's a buff you can feel! That's something you like seeing. Who cares about 13.6% more penis size or whatever? The point is that I wanna hear someone moan on it! So get some more impactful buffs. - The first few levels are too small and the stuff you find is too disinteresting. What you use that stuff for feels unclear, but not in the way that confusion supplements the horror elements. It's just annoying. Claustrophobic environment is good for horror, but not exactly super fun if you have one monster taking up a whole entire hallway. - Monsters are more annoying than scary too. - Buggy as hell, but it's Early Access, so I can forgive that. - I think having random effects like mist is a really, really cool concept. But again, afwul and unfun implementation. Who thought it was enjoyable that you have to stop and stand still for like 20 seconds every now and then, because you literally can't see anything any more? I'm giving the devs (or whoever's responsible) a lot of flack, but only because it's painful how many great ideas you can pack into something that's this boring. I hope they decide to improve this in the future. Much love to the devs, because it's obvious they have some crazy talent on their team.

I have enjoyed this game, but I can not recommend it at the moment. If a player dies, it often becomes a grind to revive them. By the time you revive them, another player will be close to death. Those deaths are often times guaranteed as medkits and consumables that regenerate health are sparse. This has created cycles I encounter often which get in the way of enjoying the game. I also dislike the open area levels where you can travel by car. There are too few points of interest to explore, and I most often find half the resources I would in an enclosed area. In cases where I needed to be revived during these levels, I could not help but be bored because I often times had to wait for upwards of half an hour to be revived. I've started asking my friends to completely skip these levels. Not out of difficulty, but because these levels are boring and not worth exploring. That is not something you want out of an exploration game. Even though you need resources to feed the elevator so that it does not eat you, I can't recall a moment where I came close to being eaten. I'm not sure what the solution here could be, but the point is that I have not felt tension from this game mechanic. I'm pretty close to liking the game, but these are issues I simply cannot overlook when I play. I really want to like this game more and hope to see them resolved.

The trailers are misleading. What they show suggests a fast-paced shooter with bosses and real exploration, but the actual game is very different. In practice, you mostly ride an elevator and go down through floors that all look the same, built with reused environments and very little variation. Every now and then you might come across themed floors inspired by things like Garry’s Mod or Akira, but they end up feeling empty and mostly decorative, without real content or rewards. Most of the game feels barren. You’ll occasionally find mines or a few enemies that are oddly overpowered, but there’s no real sense of progression. Loot never improves, and you keep getting the same few basic items that barely do any damage. Meanwhile, enemies constantly spawn in groups of three or four, chase you without stopping, and can easily kill you in one hit before you have much chance to respond. Overall, it feels unbalanced and poorly thought out, made worse by marketing that gives a completely different impression of what the game actually is.

But the trailers are composed mostly of action loaded boomer shooter set pieces that never seem to occur during runs, and they are definitely not a very good representation of the tedious Residential Block hallways players must endure at the start of each run. My impression is that the latest updates must have improved the game quite a lot, but the early game wasn't reworked to keep up. I'd really recommend you avoid this game if the trailers are what you're going by.

Originally played this game in early access and beat it with one of my friends. The game back then was kind of barren but had so much potential to be something more. Originally my friend and I had high hopes, but seeing how the game is now...I wish we never got into it. First off the trailer is incredibly misleading. You rarely will have fast past boomer shooter style battles in this game. Not only is the ai not great, but the gunplay just isn't complex enough for it. Most of your gameplay is going to consist of running through the same generated tiles looking for bottles, beer, weapons, and most importantly, fuel. Any ammo you do find you want to save for the upcoming bosses. This is fun and all, but it gradually gets super repetitive. The game seriously needs more level variety between floors, because after a while it gets grating. Enemy design is good for the most part, but I just wish the early game had more of them. Early game was a slog in early access and its even more so here. Its the worst part of the game and its a joke it hasn't been looked at or improved. Bosses for the most part suck. They're either glitchy, poorly designed, or both. Now for my biggest gripe. The car segments. Just flat out remove these. Not only do they lack resources, but they're far too large to justify their inclusion. There's just nothing to do in them, making mid to early late game a complete slog. If you're going to include them, cut down the map size by over half, and sprinkle them into the game between floors. Don't force the player to go through 6 to 8 of them. Kills all of the pacing, Additionally, the car is buggy af. A friend and I had to end a run because he and I glitched out in the car seat. Horrendous design. All and all avoid this game. There's far better friend slop games to choose from. Don't let the price of this fool you either. The game realistically has maybe 1hr of content padded out to be around 4 to 5hrs.

Если ты выкладываешь их на пол - они исчезают. Ведро сломано полностью, при попытке его починить у остальных предметов начинаются артефакты с количеством прочности, и у игрока использовавшего ведро, ломаются предметы со 100% прочностью после первого применения. При этом на ведре из-за плохо прописанного баланса, завязан весь луттинг - только у него есть большой урон при прочности, которую можно легко и дешево восстанавливать большим количеством мусора вокруг, если же пытаться ломать закрытые шкафы с предметами рукой - теряется хп, а если оружием - у любого предмета кроме ведра недостаточный урон или количество прочности, из-за чего, чтобы сломать 1 ящик ты полнсотью ломаешь об него одно оружие ближнего боя. А в ящике при этом будет в лучшем случае консерва на +14 хп, а в худшем - ничего. Казалось бы, в игре есть отмычки - вот только их падает 10-15 штук за половину прохождения, а открывают они эти ящики только с небольшим шансом. В общем поиграв вышла картина - все завязано на ведре, ведро ломает 1му из игроков использование всех предметов, а когда ты их лутаешь, сложить их все равно негде, потому что если разбросать их по лифту, наступив на них - они исчезнут, а слотов, чтобы сложить лут - нету. Атмосфера топ, но я бы ждал патчей с фиксами, если такие вообще когда-либо будут

Fun premise, but falls apart if you take the game "seriously". A single game of Kletka can last 6 hours if you're hitting every floor; maybe that's just an issue with how I'm playing the game.... but, it doesn't feel like the game incentivizes you in any way to try skipping through floors either. I see the vision: Skip ahead to keep yourself on a nice pace. The game takes your REAL time investment as the cost for playing the game..... which is..... not good? Skipping ahead puts you at a massive resource detriment, but hitting every floor puts you in a position where you have far too many resources for the game to continue to be interesting. Seems like there'd be a fine line to try and figure out, but in my experience its such a razor thin line that it might as well not exist. The new scrap mechanic they added in the recent update also just removed a lot of the difficulty from the earlier versions of the game in respect to resource scarcity. I *did* complete an entire run, so I can positively say a single run of Kletka could be half the time commitment (or even a quarter) and be much better. The interesting parts of the game are too few and far between. I had fun with it for a bit before it got stale. I hope the devs can find a happy medium over time, but its not the game for me.
